paragraphs.sourceText: Reaping the Rewards of Risk-Taking
paragraphs.translationZh: 收获冒险的回报

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Since Steve Jobs resigned as chief executive of Apple, much has been said about him as a peerless business leader who has created immense wealth for shareholders, and guided the design of hit products that are transforming entire industries, like music and mobile communications.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答）自从史蒂夫·乔布斯辞去苹果公司首席执行官职务以来，人们对他的评价是一位无与伦比的商业领袖，他为股东创造了巨大的财富，并指导了正在改变整个行业（例如音乐和移动通信）的热门产品的设计。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) All true, but let’s think different, to borrow the Apple marketing slogan of years back. Let’s look at Mr. Jobs as a role model.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 都是如此，但让我们换个角度思考，借用苹果多年前的营销口号。让我们以乔布斯先生为榜样。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Above all, he is an innovator (创新者）. His creative force is seen in products such as the iPod, iPhone, and iPad, and in new business models for pricing and distributing music and mobile software online. Studies of innovation come to the same
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 最重要的是，他是一位创新者。他的创造力体现在 iPod、iPhone 和 iPad 等产品中，以及在线定价和分销音乐和移动软件的新商业模式中。对创新的研究也得出同样的结论

paragraphs.sourceText: conclusion ：you can’t engineer innovation, but you can increase the odds of it occurring. And Mr. Jobs’ career can be viewed as a consistent pursuit of improving those odds, both for himself and the companies he has led. Mr. Jobs, of course, has enjoyed singular success. But innovation, broadly defined, is the crucial ingredient in all economic progress—higher growth for nations, more competitive products for companies, and more prosperous careers for individuals. And Mr. Jobs, many experts say, exemplifies what works in the innovation game.
paragraphs.translationZh: 结论：你无法设计创新，但你可以增加创新发生的几率。乔布斯先生的职业生涯可以被视为对提高这些可能性的不懈追求，无论是对他本人还是他所领导的公司来说都是如此。当然，乔布斯先生取得了非凡的成功。但从广义上讲，创新是所有经济进步的关键因素——国家经济增长更快，公司产品更具竞争力，个人职业生涯更繁荣。许多专家表示，乔布斯先生是创新游戏中行之有效的典范。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) “ We can look at and learn from Steve Jobs what the essence of American innovation is,” says John Kao, an innovation consultant to corporations and governments. Many other nations, Mr. John Kao notes, are now ahead of the United States in producing what are considered the raw materials of innovation. These include government financing for scientific research, national policies to support emerging industries, educational achievement, engineers and scientists graduated, even the speeds of Internet broadband service.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) “我们可以向史蒂夫·乔布斯学习美国创新的本质是什么，”企业和政府创新顾问约翰·高 (John Kao) 说道。高约翰指出，许多其他国家现在在生产创新原材料方面领先于美国。其中包括政府对科学研究的资助、国家支持新兴产业的政策、教育成就、工程师和科学家的毕业情况，甚至互联网宽带服务的速度。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Yet what other nations typically lack, Mr. Kao adds, is a social environment that encourages diversity, experimentation, risk-taking, and combining skills from many fields into products that he calls “ recombinant mash-ups ( 打碎重组),” like the iPhone, which redefined the smartphone category. “The culture of other countries doesn’t support the kind of innovation that Steve Jobs exemplifies, as America does,” Mr. John Kao says.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 然而，高先生补充道，其他国家通常缺乏的是鼓励多样性、实验、冒险以及将多个领域的技能结合到他所谓的“重组混搭”产品中的社会环境，比如重新定义了智能手机类别的 iPhone。 “其他国家的文化并不像美国那样支持史蒂夫·乔布斯所代表的那种创新，”约翰·高先生说。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Workers of every rank are told these days that wide-ranging curiosity and continuous learning are vital to thriving in the modem economy. Formal education matters, career counselors say, but real- life experience is often even more valuable.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 如今，各级工人都被告知，广泛的好奇心和持续学习对于现代经济的繁荣至关重要。职业顾问表示，正规教育很重要，但现实生活中的经验往往更有价值。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) An adopted child, growing up in Silicon Valley, Mr. Jobs displayed those traits early on. He was fascinated by electronics as a child, building Heath kit do-it-yourself projects, like radios. Mr. Jobs dropped out of Reed College after only a semester and traveled around India in search of spiritual enlightenment, before returning to Silicon Valley to found Apple with his friend, Stephen Wozniak, an engineering wizard (奇才). Mr. Jobs was forced out of Apple in 1985, went off and founded two other companies, Next and Pixar, before returning to Apple in 1996 and becoming chief executive in 1997.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 乔布斯先生是一个在硅谷长大的养子，他很早就表现出了这些特质。当他还是个孩子的时候，他就对电子产品着迷，自己动手制作 Heath 套件项目，比如收音机。乔布斯在里德学院只学习了一个学期后就退学了，他环游印度寻找精神启蒙，然后回到硅谷与他的朋友、工程奇才斯蒂芬·沃兹尼亚克一起创立了苹果公司。 1985 年，乔布斯被迫离开苹果公司，随后创立了另外两家公司：Next 和 Pixar，然后于 1996 年返回苹果公司，并于 1997 年成为首席执行官。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) His path was unique, but innovation experts say the pattern of exploration is not unusual. “It’s often people like Steve Jobs who can draw from a deep reservoir of diverse experiences that often generate breakthrough ideas and insights,” says Hal Gregersen, a professor at the European Institute of Business Administration.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 他的道路很独特，但创新专家表示，这种探索模式并不罕见。欧洲工商管理学院教授哈尔·格雷格森表示：“像史蒂夫·乔布斯这样的人往往能够从丰富的不同经验中汲取灵感，从而产生突破性的想法和见解。”

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Mr. Gregersen is a co-author of a new book, The Innovator's DNA, which is based on an eight-year study of 5000(创业者） and executives worldwide. His two collaborators and co--authors are Jeff Dyer, a professor at Brigham Young University, and Clayton Christensen, a professor at the Harvard Business School, whose 1997 book The Innovators Dilemma popularized the concept of (颠覆性的）innovation. ”
paragraphs.translationZh: I) Gregersen 先生是一本新书《创新者的 DNA》的合著者，该书基于对全球 5000 名创业者和高管长达八年的研究。他的两位合作者和合著者是杨百翰大学教授杰夫·戴尔 (Jeff Dyer) 和哈佛商学院教授克莱顿·克里斯滕森 (Clayton Christensen)，他 1997 年出版的著作《创新者困境》普及了创新的概念。 ”

paragraphs.sourceText: J) The academics identify five traits that are common to the disruptive innovators: questioning, experimenting, observing, associating and networking. Their bundle of characteristics echoes the ceaseless curiosity and willingness to take risks noted by other experts. Networking, Mr. Hal Gregersen explains, is less about career-building relationships than a consistent search for new ideas. Associating, he adds, is the ability to make idea-producing connections by linking concepts from different disciplines.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 学者们确定了颠覆性创新者的五个共同特征：质疑、实验、观察、联想和网络。他们的一系列特征与其他专家指出的不断的好奇心和冒险意愿相呼应。哈尔·格雷格森先生解释说，建立人际网络与其说是为了建立职业关系，不如说是为了不断地寻找新想法。他补充道，联想是通过将不同学科的概念联系起来，建立产生想法的联系的能力。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) “Innovators engage in these mental activities regularly,” Mr. Gregersen says. “It’s a habit for them Innovative companies, according to the authors, typically enjoy higher valuations in the stock market, which they call an “innovation premium (溢价）.” It is calculated by estimating the share of a company’s value that cannot be accounted for by its current products and cash flow. The innovation premium tries to quantify(量化)investors’ bets that a company will do even better in the future because of innovation.
paragraphs.translationZh: K）“创新者经常参与这些心理活动，”格雷格森先生说。 “这是他们的习惯。作者表示，创新型公司通常在股票市场上享有较高的估值，他们称之为“创新溢价”。它是通过估计公司当前产品和现金流无法解释的价值份额来计算的。创新溢价试图量化投资者的赌注，即公司未来会因为创新而做得更好。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Apple, by their calculations, had a 37 percent innovation premium during Mr. Jobs’ first term with the company. His years in exile resulted in a 31 percent innovation discount. After his return, Applet fortunes improved gradually at first, and improved markedly starting in 2005, yielding a 52 percent innovation premium since then.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 根据他们的计算，苹果公司在乔布斯先生在公司的第一个任期内获得了 37% 的创新溢价。他的流亡岁月导致了 31% 的创新折扣。他回归后，Applet的财富起初逐渐好转，并从2005年开始显着改善，此后产生了52%的创新溢价。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) There is no conclusive proof, but Mr. Hal Gregersen says it is unlikely that Mr. Jobs could have reshaped industries beyond computing, as he has done in his second term at Apple, without the experience outside the company, especially at Pixar—the computer-animation (动画制作）studio that created a string of critically and commercially successful movies, such as “Toy
paragraphs.translationZh: M）没有确凿的证据，但哈尔·格雷格森先生表示，如果没有公司以外的经验，特别是在皮克斯（动画制作）工作室制作了一系列评论界和商业上成功的电影，例如“玩具”，乔布斯先生不太可能像他在苹果公司的第二个任期那样重塑计算机以外的行业，就像他在苹果公司的第二个任期所做的那样。

paragraphs.sourceText: Story” and “Up.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 故事”和“向上”。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) Mr. Jobs suggested much the same thing during a commencement address to the graduating class at Stanford University in 2005. “It turned out that getting fired from Apple was the best thing that could have ever happened to me,” he told the students. Mr. Jobs also spoke of perseverance (坚持）and will power. “Sometimes life hits you in the head with a brick,” he said. “Don’t lose faith. ”
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 乔布斯先生在 2005 年斯坦福大学毕业典礼演讲中也提出了同样的建议。“事实证明，被苹果公司解雇是我一生中发生过的最好的事情，”他告诉学生们。乔布斯先生还谈到了坚持和意志力。“有时生活会用一块砖头敲你的头，”他说，“不要失去信心。”

paragraphs.sourceText: O) Mr. Jobs ended his commencement talk with a call to innovation, both in one’s choice of work and in one’s life. Be curious, experiment, take risks, he said to the students. His advice was emphasized by the words on the back of the final edition of The Whole Earth Catalog, which he quoted Stay hungry. Stay foolish. ” “And, Mr. Jobs said, “I have always wished that for myself. And now, as you graduate to begin anew, I wish that for you.
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 乔布斯先生在结束毕业演讲时呼吁人们在工作选择和生活中进行创新。他对学生们说，要保持好奇心、实验、冒险。他在《全球目录》最终版的背面引用了《保持饥饿》中的文字，强调了他的建议。保持愚蠢。 ” “而且，乔布斯先生说，“我自己也一直希望如此。现在，当你们毕业重新开始时，我希望你们也能做到这一点。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. Steve Jobs called on Stanford graduates to innovate in his commencement address.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 史蒂夫·乔布斯号召斯坦福大学的毕业生在他的毕业典礼演讲中进行创新。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. Steve Jobs considered himself lucky to have been fired once by Apple.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 史蒂夫·乔布斯认为自己很幸运，曾被苹果公司解雇过一次。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48.Steve Jobs once used computers to make movies that were commercial hits.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48.史蒂夫·乔布斯曾经用电脑制作过商业成功的电影。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. Many governments have done more than the US government in providing the raw materials for innovation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 许多政府在提供创新原材料方面比美国政府做得更多。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. Great innovators are good at connecting concepts from various academic fields.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50.伟大的创新者善于将各个学术领域的概念联系起来。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. Innovation is vital to driving economic progress.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 创新对于推动经济进步至关重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. America has a social environment that is particularly favorable to innovation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 美国的社会环境特别有利于创新。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. Innovative ideas often come from diverse experiences.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 创新想法往往来自不同的经验。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Junk food is everywhere. We’re eating way too much of it. Most of us know what we’re doing and yet we do it anyway.
paragraphs.translationZh: 垃圾食品无处不在。我们吃得太多了。我们大多数人都知道自己在做什么，但我们还是这么做了。

paragraphs.sourceText: So here’s a suggestion offered by two researchers at the Rand Corporation : Why not take a lesson from alcohol control policies and apply them to where food is sold and how it’s displayed?
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，兰德公司的两名研究人员提出了一个建议：为什么不从酒精控制政策中吸取教训，并将其应用到食品的销售地点和展示方式上呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: “Many policy measures to control obesity(肥胖症）assume that people consciously and rationally choose what and how much they eat and therefore focus on providing information and more access to healthier foods,” note the two researchers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 两位研究人员指出：“许多控制肥胖的政策措施都假设人们有意识、理性地选择吃什么和吃多少，因此专注于提供信息和更多获得健康食品的机会。”

paragraphs.sourceText: “In contrast,” the researchers continue, “ many regulations that don’t assume people make rational choices have been successfully applied to control alcohol, a substance—like food—of which immoderate consumption leads to serious health problems. ’’
paragraphs.translationZh: “相比之下，”研究人员继续说道，“许多不假设人们做出理性选择的法规已成功应用于控制酒精，酒精是一种像食物一样的物质，过度消费会导致严重的健康问题。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The research references studies of peopled behavior with food and alcohol and results of alcohol restrictions, and then lists five regulations that the researchers think might be promising if applied to junk foods. Among them:
paragraphs.translationZh: 该研究参考了人们对食物和酒精的行为以及酒精限制的结果的研究，然后列出了研究人员认为如果应用于垃圾食品可能有希望的五项法规。其中：

paragraphs.sourceText: Density restrictions：licenses to sell alcohol aren’t handed out unplanned to all comers but are allotted (分配) based on the number of places in an area that already sell alcohol. These make alcohol less easy to get and reduce the number of psychological cues to drink.
paragraphs.translationZh: 密度限制：销售酒精的许可证不会无计划地分发给所有参与者，而是根据某个地区已经销售酒精的场所数量进行分配。这些使得酒精变得不那么容易获得，并减少了饮酒的心理暗示。

paragraphs.sourceText: Similarly, the researchers say, being presented with junk food stimulates our desire to eat it. So why not limit the density of food outlets, particularly ones that sell food rich in empty calories? And why not limit sale of food in places that aren5t primarily food stores?
paragraphs.translationZh: 同样，研究人员表示，看到垃圾食品会刺激我们吃它的欲望。那么为什么不限制食品店的密度，特别是那些销售富含空热量食品的食品店呢？为什么不在主要食品店之外的地方限制食品销售呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: Display and sales restrictions: California has a rule prohibiting alcohol displays near the cash registers in gas stations, and in
paragraphs.translationZh: 展示和销售限制：加利福尼亚州有一项规定，禁止在加油站和其他地方的收银台附近展示酒精饮料

paragraphs.sourceText: most places you can’t buy alcohol at drive-through facilities. At supermarkets, food companies pay to have their wares in places where they’re easily seen. One could remove junk food to the back of the store and ban them from the shelves at checkout lines. The other measures include restricting portion sizes, taxing and prohibiting special price deals for junk foods, and placing warning labels on the products.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在大多数地方，您不能在免下车服务设施中购买酒精饮料。在超市，食品公司付费将商品放在容易看到的地方。人们可以把垃圾食品移到商店后面，并禁止它们出现在收银台的货架上。其他措施包括限制份量、对垃圾食品征税和禁止特价交易，以及在产品上贴上警告标签。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Kodak’s decision to file for bankruptcy (破产）protection is a sad, though not unexpected, turning point for a leading American corporation that pioneered consumer photography and dominated the film market for decades, but ultimately failed to adapt to the digital revolution.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于一家美国领先公司来说，柯达申请破产保护的决定是一个悲伤但并不意外的转折点，该公司是消费摄影的先驱，并主导了胶片市场数十年，但最终未能适应数字革命。

paragraphs.sourceText: Although many attribute Kodak’s downfall to “complacency ( 自满)”that explanation doesn’t acknowledge the lengths to which the company went to reinvent itself. Decades ago, Kodak anticipated that digital photography would overtake film—and in fact, Kodak invented the first digital camera in 1975—but in a fateful decision, the company chose to shelf its new discovery to focus on its traditional film business.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管许多人将柯达的垮台归咎于“自满”，但这种解释并没有承认该公司为重塑自身而付出的努力。几十年前，柯达预计数码摄影将取代胶片——事实上，柯达在 1975 年发明了第一台数码相机——但该公司做出了一个重大决定，选择搁置其新发现，专注于其传统胶片业务。

paragraphs.sourceText: It wasn’t that Kodak was blind to the future, said Rebecca Henderson, a professor at Harvard Business School, but rather that it failed to execute on a strategy to confront it. By the time the company realized its mistake, it was too late.
paragraphs.translationZh: 哈佛商学院教授丽贝卡·亨德森表示，这并不是柯达对未来视而不见，而是它未能执行应对未来的战略。当公司意识到自己的错误时，为时已晚。

paragraphs.sourceText: Kodak is an example of a firm that was very much aware that they had to adapt, and spent a lot of money trying to do so, but ultimately failed. Large companies have a difficult time switching to new markets because there is a temptation to put existing assets into the new businesses.
paragraphs.translationZh: 柯达就是一个例子，该公司非常清楚自己必须适应，并花费了大量资金试图做到这一点，但最终失败了。大公司很难转向新市场，因为存在将现有资产投入新业务的诱惑。

paragraphs.sourceText: Although Kodak anticipated the inevitable rise of digital photography, its corporate(企业的）culture was too rooted in the successes of the past for it to make the clean break necessary to fully embrace the future. They were a company stuck in time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管柯达预见到数码摄影将不可避免地崛起，但其企业文化过于植根于过去的成功，以至于无法彻底决裂以全面拥抱未来。他们是一家被困在时间里的公司。

paragraphs.sourceText: Their history was so important to them. Now their history has become a liability.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他们的历史对他们来说非常重要。现在，他们的历史已成为一种负担。

paragraphs.sourceText: Kodak’s downfall over the last several decades was dramatic. In 1976, the company commanded 90% of the market for photographic film and 85% of the market for cameras. But the 1980s brought new competition from Japanese film company Fuji Photo, which undermined Kodak by offering lower prices for film and photo supplies. Kodak’s decision not to pursue the role of official film for the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics was a major miscalculation. The bid went instead to Fuji, which exploited its sponsorship to win a permanent foothold in the marketplace.
paragraphs.translationZh: 柯达在过去几十年里的衰落是戏剧性的。 1976年，该公司占据了胶片市​​场90%的份额和相机市场85%的份额。但 20 世纪 80 年代，日本胶片公司富士胶片带来了新的竞争，该公司通过降低胶片和照片耗材的价格削弱了柯达的实力。柯达决定不担任 1984 年洛杉矶奥运会的官方胶片是一个重大误判。最终竞标的是富士，后者利用其赞助在市场上赢得了永久的立足点。
